newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lebed aide dismisses talk of Russia coup plot.
newsitem.headline: Lebed aide dismisses talk of Russia coup plot.

text.p: A senior aide to Russian security tsar Alexander Lebed on Wednesday dismissed allegations that the outspoken Security Council secretary was plotting to use force to seize power.

"(The accusations) are, to say the least, not serious," Security Council press secretary Alexander Barkhatov told Interfax news agency after Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov had accused Lebed, his main rival, of trying to take over the reins of power.
The suspects, who were between 26 and 51 years old, had in part confessed to the crime, prosecutor Reiner Schilling said. One of the women had worked in Fiszmann's property firm for 10 years.

"These are the main suspects," Klaus-Juergen Timm, the head of criminal investigations in the state of Hesse, told journalists. "But we are not ruling out the possibility that there were more perpetrators."
The ransom money was found in the garden of a flat in Wiesbaden, with two 2,000-mark ($1,300) notes missing.
The authorities have said they believed that Fiszmann was still alive even though the kidnappers had reneged on a promise to free him after the ransom was paid last week.
